name: virtualized-table
title: Virtualized table
description: Thousands of rows rendered as a few dozen: a windowed table with a fixed row height, a sticky header and true row counts for screen readers.
docs: Every row is the same height (`rowHeight`, default 44) and a cell is one line; longer content is cut with an ellipsis, because a taller row would make the scrollbar lie. Keep rows times rowHeight below about 15 million pixels (a few hundred thousand rows at 44px): browsers cap the height of an element. `aria-rowcount` is the number of rows plus the header, so a screen reader says "row 4,813 of 12,431" for the 4,812th row. Selection plugs in through `getRowProps` (return `data-state="selected"`) and sorting through a column's `sort` and `onSort`, which turn the header into the Table's sort button. Use `getRowKey` when rows are sorted or filtered, `onRangeChange` to load the next page near the end, and a CSS length such as "60vh" for `height`. A column's `cell` is a function, so use the table from a Client Component; columns that only name a key (`id` and a text `header`) also work from a Server Component. Find-in-page cannot see rows that are not rendered.
